prompt: In a trigraph, let $u,v,x$ be distinct vertices. Merge $u,v$ into a new vertex $w$. Write $B,N,R$ for black edge, non-edge, and red edge, respectively; a status pair records $ux$ and $vx$. What is the status of $wx$?

answers.text: $BB\mapsto B$, $NN\mapsto N$; every other pair of statuses maps to $R$.
answers.explanation: Both parts must agree definitely to yield a definite edge or non-edge. Any disagreement or inherited uncertainty stays red.

answers.text: $BB\mapsto B$, $NN\mapsto N$, $BN\mapsto N$; inherited red edges stay red.
answers.explanation: An edge/non-edge disagreement must become red; choosing non-edge loses the discrepancy.

answers.text: $BB\mapsto B$, $NN\mapsto N$, $BN\mapsto B$; inherited red edges stay red.
answers.explanation: Taking the union of neighbourhoods hides an edge/non-edge disagreement instead of recording it.
Agreement of two black edges stays black, and agreement of two non-edges stays a non-edge.
Two red incidences do not cancel their inherited uncertainty.
A black edge does not resolve the uncertainty inherited from the red edge.
A definite non-edge does not resolve uncertainty from a red incidence.

answers.text: $BB\mapsto R$, $NN\mapsto N$; every remaining pair maps to $R$.
answers.explanation: Two complete adjacency relations combine into another complete relation, so black plus black is black.

answers.text: $BB\mapsto B$, $NN\mapsto R$; every remaining pair maps to $R$.
answers.explanation: Two empty adjacency relations combine into an empty relation, so non-edge plus non-edge stays a non-edge.

answers.text: Equal statuses are preserved; unequal statuses map to the status of $ux$.
answers.explanation: The merge is symmetric in its two inputs. Different definite statuses must produce red, independent of order.

sources.title: Bonnet et al. — Twin-width I, §§2–4 (2021 version)
